page: Vultr vx1-m-64c-512gb belongs to the VX1 Cloud Compute family and provides a high-density, memory-optimized architecture. The server is driven by a 2.0 GHz AMD EPYC x86_64 processor delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs from 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 512 GB of total system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache and 1 MB of L2 cache per core. Local storage is limited to a bundled 1 GB NVMe SSD, while connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Architectural extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, SHA_NI, and VAES acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core computational throughput and memory bandwidth. The instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 28,469 and a Passmark CPU score of 98,920.13, coupled with a Clang compilation score of 64,319. Memory benchmarks highlight high data velocity, recording 532.73 GB/sec during large-block uncached read operations and 251.91 GB/sec in write operations. Operational throughput tests show 111.5 million Redis SET operations per second and small-model LLM prompt processing speeds of 5,494.4 tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of the server profile is the minimal 1 GB local NVMe storage volume, which requires external storage configurations for workloads requiring persistent disk I/O. However, the high ratio of 512 GB RAM to 64 dedicated compute cores delivers efficient multi-threaded density. This profile is well suited for large in-memory caching layers, Redis clusters, real-time database operations, distributed software compilation, and CPU-bound machine learning inference.
description: Vultr vx1-m-64c-512gb is a memory-optimized cloud compute instance built for high-throughput computational and in-memory tasks. Powered by a 2.0 GHz AMD EPYC processor, it features 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores and 512 GB of RAM, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. Local bundled storage is limited to a 1 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmark data exhibits top-tier capability, with 532.73 GB/sec uncached read memory bandwidth, a Passmark CPU score of 98,920.13, and 111.5 million Redis SET operations per second. Supported by AVX-512 vector instruction sets, it excels at memory-heavy operations while requiring external storage for high-capacity data persistence. The instance fits in-memory databases, Redis caches, Clang compilation, and CPU-driven inference.
